after:
Stem I (—/rukzi (belegt: Infectum 3pl; Grundform ungesichert)): 1: sich niederlassen, sich ansiedeln
Stem II (mrakzile (belegt: Preterit, Objekt 3pl)/— (Grundformen ungesichert)): 1: (Personen) zur Ordnung bringen, zurechtbringen

new_senses.rationale: Return to Midyat followed by d rukzi distinguishes establishing residence from merely arriving. One attested plural Infectum; stem and base forms remain provisional.

added_examples.turoyo: W hawi u ṣulḥ baynoṯayye, bale lə səmme ǧasara d oṯən b ḥḏo naqla l Məḏyaḏ w d rukzi.
added_examples.translation: So kam es zum Frieden zwischen ihnen, doch (die Christen) wagten es nicht, auf einen Schlag nach Midyat zurückzukehren und sich niederzulassen.
added_examples.rationale: First proposed I Infectum example; settlement is distinguished from return in the same clause.

new_senses.rationale: Mrakzile is followed by bringing the monks to the right path and preaching to them. Provisionally transitive II; exact lexical breadth and object segmentation remain open.

added_examples.turoyo: komər yatu mrakzile, manṭalle lu darbo, w krəzle aʕlayye, hawxa yo hawxa yo hawxa yo.
added_examples.translation: Er ließ sich nieder, disziplinierte sie und brachte sie wieder auf den rechten Weg, und er predigte ihnen: (Es verhält sich) so und so und so.
added_examples.rationale: First proposed II Preterit example; following right-path and preaching predicates support ordering people.

rationale: New entry proposal based on two occurrences in different texts. No etymology is asserted: an Arabic connection is only a reader's hypothesis.; I has only Infectum 3pl rukzi, governed by d- and sharing returning Christians as subject; Midyat is the understood settlement location. No Preterit base form can be recovered securely.; II has only mrakzile, provisionally analysed as a masculine singular Preterit actor with plural object before -le. Yatu is a separate preceding verb, not proof that mrakzile means settle oneself.; Forms fields record attested inflections and explicitly leave unattested base forms open. No complete paradigm, Detransitive, or idiom is invented.
